source.name: NASA NSSDCA Planetary Fact Sheet (metric) and Sun/Earth Comparison
source.note: Sheet 'Last Updated: 13 November 2026'. Moon counts change as new moons are confirmed. Moon distance is from Earth, not the Sun.

bodies.name: Sun
bodies.fact: The Sun holds about 99.8% of all the mass in the solar system.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.fact: A single day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts longer than its year.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.fact: Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.fact: Earth is the only place we know of with liquid water on its surface and life.

bodies.name: Moon
bodies.fact: The Moon always shows the same face to Earth.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.fact: Mars is red because iron minerals in its dust have rusted.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.fact: Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet: under 10 hours.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.fact: Saturn is less dense than water.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.fact: Uranus spins on its side, tilted about 98 degrees.

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.fact: Neptune takes about 164 Earth years to go round the Sun once.

quiz.hint: It is not the closest one. Think thick clouds.
It is the fifth from the Sun.

quiz.q: Which planet has the most moons?
quiz.hint: It also has the most famous rings.
